checks.evidence_note: psi-map.json maps seed 'same' to accession PSI-102
PSI-102.search.json Title 'Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment' and Acronym 'SAME'
SAME from PSI acronym; SAME-1 and Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment are common variants consistent with the title
Schema enum includes 'same'; seed id is 'same'
PSI flightProgram 'International Space Station (ISS)' and investigation dates 2001-2008 confirm flown status
PSI-102.json and PSI-102.search.json exist locally; accession confirmed in psi-map.json
Standard PSI URL pattern for accession PSI-102; psi-map.json does not supply URL but pattern is documented
PSI-102.search.json Flight Platform 'International Space Station (ISS)'; NASA page confirms MSG in Destiny lab; PSI-102.json experimentHardware 'Comparitive Soot Diagnostic Hardware' operated in MSG
PSI-102.search.json Objectives and PSI-102.json objective match the extracted text; NASA page and NIST publication confirm smoke particle size characterization for detector evaluation
Challenge brief explicitly states fire detection tested via SAME/SAME-R; NASA page confirms evaluation of ionisation and photoelectric detectors

NASA page: four solid spacecraft materials plus liquid DBP on wick; Meyer et al. (2018) confirms four solids + liquid reference material; oxidative pyrolysis not flaming combustion, so 'mixed' is correct

NASA page lists 5 materials (Teflon, Kapton, silicone rubber, cellulose, DBP on wick). Meyer et al. (2018) adds Pyrell (polyurethane foam). SAME final report lists same 5 as NASA. Pyrell may be from SAME-R or ground tests; not confirmed in SAME flight data. List of 6 is plausible but not fully supported by primary SAME sources.
SAME final report: samples heated by stainless-steel wire coil, six pre-weighed samples per rotatable carousel; DBP on porous wick. NIST/NASA news confirms wire filaments and carousel.
SAME final report and NASA page both state Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) on ISS in Destiny laboratory.

NASA page and SAME final report both describe smoke generation duct with carousel, aging chamber with piston, diagnostics duct with P-Trak, DustTraks, modified ionisation detector, thermal precipitator (TEM grids), and ISS/Shuttle smoke detectors.
PSI-102.search.json Related Investigations lists PSI-101 (SAME-R). Challenge brief states SAME/SAME-R instrument used for DAFT/DAFT-2 dust detection.
PSI experimental table (PSI-102.csv) has no O2 column; no source states chamber O2 for SAME. Null with unknown confidence is correct.
PSI experimental table has no pressure column; no source states chamber pressure for SAME. Null with unknown confidence is correct.
PSI-102.csv column 'Air Flow (cm/s)' shows values 5 and 10 across 8 test rows; min 5, max 10 cm/s matches extracted range.

Extracted as min 0, max 0 g based on ISS platform = microgravity. PSI-102.search.json Project Type 'Microgravity Investigation' and Flight Platform ISS support microgravity context. However, no source states a measured g-level; value is a platform-based deduction (inferred). Confidence 'medium' is appropriate but note should clarify inference.
No source identifies a combustion-chamber diluent. Nitrogen appears only as sheath gas for P-Trak particle counter, not as test condition. Null with unknown confidence is correct.

NASA page: different airflow rates, heating temperatures, aging durations. Meyer et al.: controlled parameters were heating temperature, air flow, aging duration. SAME final report: aging 10 s to 1800 s. All four listed variables confirmed.

SAME final report: sample heating time ~60 s, air flow synchronized for steady stream. Meyer et al.: baseline temperature chosen for 1-2 mg mass loss in 60 s, holding mass loss roughly constant. Apparatus and instrumentation held constant across tests.

NASA page lists P-Trak, DustTrak, modified ionisation detector, thermal precipitator (TEM), ISS and Shuttle detectors. Meyer et al. confirms three real-time instruments, ionisation detector for first moment, thermal precipitator, ISS/Shuttle detectors. NASA news confirms MPASS two-moment sensor on SAME reflight (SAME-2).

Challenge brief names SAME/SAME-R for fire detection. NIST/NASA news states ISS photoelectric detector missed smaller Teflon and Kapton smoke particles; no single current method detects all smoke sizes.
NASA page: detectors useful in submarines/underwater labs. NASA news: nuisance-free detectors for homes; MPASS sensor for first responders, mines, factories.

All five publication entries are real SAME-related works verifiable via DOIs and NTRS: SAE 2008-01-2089, Aerosol Sci Tech 2015, Fire Safety J 98 (2018), AIAA 2012-3536, NASA TM final report. PSI-102.search.json Publication Title list includes matching titles.
psi-map.json maps 'same' to PSI-102; PSI-102.json and PSI-102.search.json both have accession PSI-102.
PSI-102.search.json Project Type 'Microgravity Investigation'; PSI-102.json projectType 'Microgravity Investigation'. Simplified to 'Microgravity' per schema.

Only fuel_materials (Pyrell inclusion not confirmed in primary SAME flight sources) and gravity_g (platform-based deduction, not measured) received 'partly' verdicts. No contradictions found.
